name: ROCKWELL COLLINS, INC.
brief_text:
Three detectors fired for Rockwell Collins. Benford's Law analysis of leading digits in award amounts showed a statistically significant deviation from expected frequency distribution, with observed digit-1 frequency of 27.4% versus expected 30.1%, suggesting possible non-random award structuring. Modification growth on contract W15P7T16D0003 expanded at an extreme rate relative to engineering-services peers, with a growth ratio of 32,947 compared to a peer average of 124. The Isolation Forest multivariate test flagged the entity as a statistical outlier based on its combined profile of total dollars, award volume, and modification patterns.

The Benford test yielded a KS statistic of 0.051 with p-value 0.039 across 762 transactions. The modification-growth z-score reached 19.8 sigma, far exceeding the typical 3-sigma threshold for anomaly. The isolation anomaly score was 0.921 on a 0-to-1 scale, indicating strong multivariate deviation. The entity shows a 9.4% competition ratio and 63.9% modification frequency, with all 762 awards concentrated in a single awarding agency.

These statistical signals warrant scrutiny but do not confirm fraud. Rockwell Collins is a large, established defense contractor with $4.9 billion in lifetime obligations, which may explain high modification frequency and sole-agency concentration in legitimate program contexts. The Benford deviation is modest in absolute terms and may reflect industry-standard contract structures. The extreme modification-growth z-score on a single contract deserves investigation, though large defense programs routinely experience scope changes. Small peer-group size in specialized engineering services may inflate z-scores.
